purpose: Bound how far a bound-invariance verdict read under perfect play carries. Every cap-fitting cell folds exactly once, so the published verdicts were all read in the one-fold regime; these cells fold repeatedly, which is where a stalling controller can carry extra entries into a LATER summarize input and reach a cap the oracle transcript never touches.
why_not_cap_fitting: A second fold needs the post-fold prompt to cross the FULL guard, because trigger hysteresis raises the trigger to 1.0 after the first summary. A fold replaces at least one transcript entry with a strictly shorter summary line, so the post-fold prompt is below the walk's own peak -- and a cap-fitting guard is ABOVE that peak by construction. A repeatedly folding cell therefore lives below the cap peak, where the observation_cap arm overflows, and the fixture declares the compact arm only.

margin_scaling.why: The imperfect-play margin is budgeted extra steps times the size of one wasted-step entry, so it is a property of the STEP BUDGET and not the constant a single study's margin makes it look like. Reading it at three step budgets is what says which of the two it is.

cells.why: Perfect play folds twice and both bounds offer the summarizer the identical bytes, so the oracle walk calls the cell bound-invariant. The stalling walk spends its whole step budget, grows the post-fold transcript far enough for a THIRD fold, and that fold's offered transcript finally outgrows the trigger bound's cap while the window bound still clears it -- so the two bounds stop sending the same prompts on a transcript the oracle never produced.

The control. It folds repeatedly under BOTH walks with the identical offered transcripts, so its verdict is invariant under both -- which is what keeps the separating cell above a finding about this geometry rather than a worst-case pass that reports every repeatedly folding cell as changed.
